correspondence.component_scope: Selected headward opening and southern turn
correspondence.finding: The selected first approach and south-to-northeast turn are not traceable on the readable original maps at adequate ordinary corridor scale. No Ranchería, La Quebrada, reservoir or formal source name is assigned to this opening.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper northeast approach into the receiving valley
correspondence.finding: The broad approach lies within the study setting, but the complete selected route and its entry into the named receiving river remain insufficiently distinguished from the adjoining tributary network. Basin membership and station proximity are not through-link proof.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle receiving corridor
correspondence.finding: The sequence of the middle valley, separate side approaches and mapped receiving course supports Río Ranchería as a bounded receiving-system candidate. Detailed source curves and the selected generalized line are not treated as exact-bank matches; this partial correspondence does not certify every stored join.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern turn, lower split and northwest continuation
correspondence.finding: Regional coverage supports the broad lower-river setting, but does not establish the selected passage through every fork and its reunion. The named left/right arms cannot be substituted for the selected path without correspondence. The northwest continuation remains only regionally supported.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual coastal endpoint
correspondence.finding: A river-to-Caribbean relationship is contextual evidence only. The actual selected final coastal continuation, distributary and sea-class terminal are not independently matched. The endpoint is not moved to an adjacent mouth, lagoon or familiar delta label.

correspondence.component_scope: Waterbody or managed transfers
correspondence.finding: No selected reservoir or lagoon traversal is demonstrated. The report’s mention of El Cercado elsewhere in the basin does not establish that the chosen path passes through it. No current flow, control structure operation, canal connection or exact shoreline inference is made.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen opening and eastward inland-ice sequence
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening lies in the mapped Inland Ice south of the Dronning Louise Land exposed-rock belt. Its short initial southward leg and subsequent eastward-to-northeastward parts are covered through the surrounding ice and small exposed-rock outliers to the southern rock-margin approach. The complete first thirteen parts and their joins are geographically accounted for; ice contours and isolated nunataks do not establish a natural river.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern Dronning Louise Land ice and exposed-rock margin
correspondence.finding: The eastward continuation and small southward reverse bend occupy the generalized ice/exposed-rock margin at the southern end of Dronning Louise Land. All selected short parts are visible in contiguous original cartography. The source differentiates ice from the colored rock units, but does not show this whole selected succession as a named river or establish hydraulic through-links between its parts.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward turn and intervening ice/rock corridor
correspondence.finding: The sharp northward departure and successive short steps cross the generalized exposed-rock and intervening ice-margin corridor on the eastern side of the southern Dronning Louise Land belt. The source covers each selected turn and intermediate join. Terrain correspondence does not prove a channel across the rock/ice sequence, a lake outlet or subglacial continuity.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeastward succession into the broad lower-ice setting
correspondence.finding: Every part of the northeastward succession is covered along the exposed-rock and ice margin toward the broader ice-covered corridor east of Dronning Louise Land. The original distinguishes the neighboring bedrock blocks and ice passages. No selected lake-throughflow, reservoir or managed-channel connector, representative river identity or continuous watercourse is established.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower ice approach toward the southwestern Dove Bugt setting
correspondence.finding: The complete northeastward approach is exposed in the broad mapped ice corridor east of Dronning Louise Land, in the southern vicinity of the Storstrømmen regional label and toward southwestern Dove Bugt. The original covers all ten small parts and their joins with the preceding rock-margin sequence and final northward approach. Storstrømmen is contextual ice geography here, not a verified reach name or whole-river identity.

correspondence.component_scope: Final northward part and actual selected terminal
correspondence.finding: The entire long penultimate part, its final northward steps, the last short stored part and the actual rendered endpoint are covered at the historical mapped ice/coastal-water margin on the southwestern Dove Bugt side. The original distinguishes the ice tongue, neighboring exposed-rock islands and coastal water. The supplied source and rendered endpoints lie in that same ordinary terminal setting. Neither the model’s sea-terminal classification nor the nearby bay label establishes an ordinary river mouth. Exact modern ice-front or bank placement and exact present ice/land/water assignment are not asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Short northern headward approach above Little Cienaga
correspondence.finding: The source depicts Cienaga Seca Creek below Little Cienaga and a small spring/tributary drainage on the adjacent slope. The chosen initial hillside approach is not independently established over its full short extent by this view; the nearby creek name is not assigned to the opening merely by proximity.

correspondence.component_scope: Cienaga Seca Creek to Santa Ana River near Heart Bar
correspondence.finding: After the initial approach, the chosen corridor follows the westward Cienaga Seca Creek valley beside State Route 38. The original depicts its connection with Santa Ana River in the Heart Bar area and the receiving river continuing northwest. Cienaga Seca Creek remains a separate reach name.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Santa Ana River through Seven Oaks and the mountain canyon
correspondence.finding: The labeled Santa Ana River continues through the selected mountain valley, including the Seven Oaks settlement setting and mapped tributary junctions. The selected bends remain within the same river-canyon corridor at the intended regional scale; the original does not require a transfer to an adjacent drainage.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower mountain canyon and dam near Warm Springs
correspondence.finding: Overlapping originals show Santa Ana River in the narrowing canyon, the mapped dam at its lower end near Warm Springs, and the downstream river exiting toward the lowland wash. This supports the ordinary dam-and-river passage; current releases, water level and operating behavior are not established.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern lowland Santa Ana wash and Mill Creek junction
correspondence.finding: The map shows Santa Ana River leaving the canyon and receiving Mill Creek, then extending west through the broad wash. The eastern and central selected interval corresponds to that wash. Its later northwest departure toward the pond terrain is treated separately in C06.

correspondence.component_scope: East Highland pond/excavation detour toward Plunge Creek
correspondence.finding: The selected late part 11 and part 12 leave the mapped Santa Ana River wash and cross pond/excavation terrain toward Plunge Creek near the Foothill Freeway. The higher-detail original clearly maps Santa Ana River to the south, Plunge Creek to the north, and their downstream confluence to the west. It does not depict a through-channel across the selected intervening terrain. The lower Plunge Creek-to-Santa Ana junction is mapped, but it does not prove the preceding selected cross-link.

correspondence.component_scope: San Bernardino, Colton and the southwest-turning river corridor
correspondence.finding: Downstream of the mapped Plunge Creek junction, the source follows the named Santa Ana River through the urban wash and past the mapped tributary network toward Colton, then around the southwest bend. Generalized straight segments and displaced bends are assessed as corridor correspondence, not exact bank registration.

correspondence.component_scope: Riverside, Jurupa Valley and Norco
correspondence.finding: Overlapping maps depict the continuous Santa Ana River corridor southwest past Riverside and then west through its meanders and vegetated floodplain toward Norco. Nearby canals are separately drawn. The selected route corresponds to the river corridor without requiring an inferred interbasin or canal transfer.

correspondence.component_scope: Prado Flood Control Basin and Prado Dam
correspondence.finding: The original depicts Santa Ana River entering the Prado wetland/flood-control setting, the adjoining Mill Creek and Chino Creek water network, rectangular managed ponds, and the impounded basin ending at Prado Dam. The selected passage lies within this mapped connected river/basin setting and emerges into the named downstream Santa Ana River. This is ordinary basin-scale passage evidence, not proof of an exact operating route through individual pond cells.

correspondence.component_scope: Downstream Santa Ana canyon to the Yorba Linda and Anaheim setting
correspondence.finding: Overlapping originals show the river downstream of Prado following the canyon near State Route 91 and continuing into the lower urban plain. The named river, canyon bends, tributary joins and adjacent canals remain distinguishable; the selected line is generalized within that corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: Anaheim, Orange and Santa Ana urban river
correspondence.finding: The source depicts the broad river and managed-water corridor bending south through the Anaheim and Orange setting and continuing beside Santa Ana. The mapped river stays distinct from nearby off-channel basins and the separate Santiago Creek network. The selected corridor can be followed continuously at the ordinary map scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Santa Ana River and actual coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The original labels Santa Ana River along the lower channel to Pacific Coast Highway and the open Pacific coast between the Huntington Beach and Newport Beach settings. Huntington Beach Channel and the adjacent coastal marsh/slough are separately depicted. The actual selected terminal is at this river-mouth coastal setting, not Newport Bay. Exact shoreline, jetty alignment and the rendered offshore extension are outside the bounded correspondence claim.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southeastern opening and westward unnamed feeder
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening follows the mapped unnamed tributary valley northward, rounds its eastern bend, then turns west to meet the northward South Fork Buckland River corridor. The original depicts the connected channel and junction; the name of this small feeder is not established. The selected opening is a chosen model start, not a verified natural spring or official river source.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper South Fork Buckland River and northern turn
correspondence.finding: Repeated direct South Fork Buckland River labels identify the mapped receiving trunk. It continues north through the selected meanders and successive smaller tributary joins, then turns northwest into the middle-view overlap. Nearby lakes and abandoned-channel shapes are not treated as required through-lake passages.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwest South Fork reach and Middle/North Fork junction setting
correspondence.finding: The source shows the selected northwest-trending South Fork continuously through its meander corridor, the separately named Middle Fork approach from the east, and the North Fork approach from the north. The mapped joins connect into the downstream channel labeled Buckland River. These incoming fork names are not substituted for the selected South Fork approach, and no exact formal name-transition vertex is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle Buckland River meanders and West Fork junction
correspondence.finding: Repeated Buckland River labels and continuous mapped channels support the selected northwest course and its large westward bend. The lower-view overlap shows the separate West Fork Buckland River joining from the south and the receiving trunk continuing west. Floodplain ponds and oxbows are distinguishable from the through-channel.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward trunk, northern bend and Buckland settlement reach
correspondence.finding: The original shows the selected western trunk turning north and northwest through the same connected valley, past successive creek joins and the labeled Buckland settlement. The generalized model cuts across some large bends, but ordinary corridor identity remains clear. No reservoir or selected lake crossing needs an inferred connector.

correspondence.component_scope: Final broad lower-river branches and actual selected endpoint
correspondence.finding: North of Buckland settlement the mapped river widens and branches around islands and wetland-rich floodplain. The selection follows this connected lower-river corridor and ends within its western/northern channel at a major branching setting. Mapped water continues beyond the selected endpoint. This endpoint is not presented as the river mouth, shoreline, bay entry or end of the complete natural Buckland River.
